competing_explanations: Actual message semantics affect the monitor output.
Event inclusion, completeness cues, prompt length, or deterministic presentation explain most response changes.
Synthetic B5 results differ because the synthetic request compiler and matrix/regret distribution do not match the production M4 B5 path.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: For all 24 assigned contexts, compare all three raw-label pairs: Public-only vs Privileged-neutral, Privileged-neutral vs Privileged-original, and Public-only vs Privileged-original. Predeclare the package-dominant, text-substitution-dominant, and ambiguous count patterns; report provider token differences and keep message meaning, length, wording, and salience confounded within the text-substitution contrast. Separately run the 40-row balanced synthetic compiler/arithmetic/enum-order diagnostic.
candidates.hypothesis: Across the 24 fixed M4 contexts, B5 label changes will be more frequent between Public-only and Privileged-neutral views than between Privileged-original and Privileged-neutral views. This would indicate that the historical response change is more associated with the bundled evidence-view package than with the message-text substitution alone; it would not establish semantic comprehension or collusion.
candidates.selection_note: Selected for the approved, bounded M4 B5 context-sensitivity monitor campaign. The broad context-access question overlaps Arike et al.; claims remain limited to fixed-case response sensitivity to evidence-view packaging and message-text substitution, not semantic comprehension or collusion. A2 is a synthetic compiler/arithmetic/enum-order diagnostic, not a population capability estimate. Protocol and registration are being frozen before dispatch.
candidates.title: Which part of privileged evidence changes B5 public-harm responses?

competing_explanations: The extra chat-stage prompt or target salience, rather than delivered message meaning, causes the finite package contrast.
Shared-target knowledge allows parallel choices; the observed interaction may depend on payoff-family features rather than communication.
The post-hoc pattern is specific to the current Qwen3 checkpoint, scenario families, or assignment sequence and will not reproduce in new matched groups.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: Before any new response, freeze three new output-independent payoff matrices, 15 new matched scenario/seed groups, all five original conditions, and a counterbalanced order. Recompute target execution from ballots and estimate the four-cell interaction on all assigned groups. A null/negative interaction, failures concentrated in a condition, or a result confined to one family weakens a general package claim. Message-semantic effects remain outside this contrast and require separate randomization.
candidates.hypothesis: In a prospective matched replication, the assigned private-target-reward plus chat-stage package will produce a positive target-execution interaction relative to private reward without chat and chat without private reward. This hypothesis concerns the treatment package only; it does not predict that message semantics, agreement, collusion, or intent are identified.
candidates.selection_note: Selected as the next prospective scientific question after the post-hoc M1-100 factorial reanalysis: the assigned private-reward/chat-stage package had target execution in 9/15 matched groups versus 0/15 in each other 2x2 cell. This is finite descriptive evidence only; it is heterogeneous by payoff family, does not isolate message semantics, and is not confirmatory. A prospective replication protocol and fresh experiment-specific approval are required before any Agent call.
candidates.title: Does a private target reward interact with chat-stage availability in allocation choices?

competing_explanations: The exact-request label disagreements are present in raw model tool-call arguments, and independent strict parsing reproduces each stored label.
Raw arguments have matching labels while differences appear in stored predictions, parsing, or row association.
Raw response bodies or ancillary argument fields differ while the binary label remains the same.
A frozen request, response, or model-fingerprint integrity check fails and invalidates affected comparisons.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: For the complete 48-pair historical/current exact-request and matching-reported-fingerprint schedule, independently strict-parse each raw report_evidence tool call and compare labels and evidence refs with the stored result. Preserve all missing, malformed, or mismatched rows; do not inspect labels during schedule selection.
candidates.hypothesis: Among the 48 preselected historical/current B5 pairs with byte-identical request bodies and matching reported system fingerprints, any stored label disagreement will also be present in raw model tool-call arguments, and an independent strict parser will reproduce both stored labels. A parser or scorer mismatch would falsify this hypothesis.
candidates.selection_note: Selected as a zero-call measurement-integrity test for the Tier 1 B5 evidence-view instability question. It can determine whether already reported finite label disagreement exists in raw responses or is introduced downstream; it is not a standalone scientific contribution and cannot explain which input cue caused the historical 20/24 paired changes.
candidates.title: Does exact-request B5 label disagreement originate in raw responses or downstream mapping?
